title: Material karma in the destiny matrix: the old habit behind your money

seo.title: Material karma in the destiny matrix: calculation and meaning
seo.description: Material karma in the destiny matrix: calculate your three numbers, understand C, Q and L, and see how this line differs from the karmic tail.
queries: material karma in the destiny matrix
material karma and the money line

meaning: Material karma is a set of three points on the right-hand spoke of the destiny matrix: C, Q and L. Read them from the outer corner towards the centre. C is the Material task, the arcanum of your birth year: the area where your habitual way of handling money, possessions and energy works against you. Q is your Attitude to the material: what you think and feel about it. L is the Entry of the money line: where the theme turns into earnings, and where it can get stuck. You can calculate all three from your date of birth in a couple of minutes: L = C + centre, Q = C + L. Reduce any sum above 22 by adding its digits. There are 246 possible triples. This line is distinct from both the karmic tail and the money channel, although it shares one point with the money channel: L.

Three common sources of confusion. First, it is not just your birth-year number. The birth-year arcanum is only the first point. Some calculators and articles show that number alone and call it material karma. In Yuliana Lisovskaya’s approach, the line has three points, with the other two developing the first. Second, it is not the karmic tail or the money channel. The tail is the lower spoke, M–N–D; the money line is L–R2–R. Material karma shares one point with the money line and none with the tail. The same numbers mean different things on these lines. Third, it is not a debt from a past life. Lisovskaya links the line to past incarnations, but that is her belief, rather than a conclusion drawn from a birth date. In essence, the line describes a familiar pattern you follow on autopilot until you notice it.

paragraphs: Your triple appears as soon as you calculate your chart, both on the diagram and in the ‘Material karma’ section. The numbers are free to view; the meaning of each arcanum in its role is explained below in this article.

article_sections.h2: Where to find material karma in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: The destiny matrix is drawn as an eight-pointed star. The main square has four corners: birth day A on the left, month B at the top, year C on the right and Karmic task D at the bottom. E is the centre. Material karma runs along the **right-hand spoke**, from the birth-year corner towards the centre. It contains three points. C is the outer corner itself, L is closest to the centre, and Q sits between them.

Moving outwards from the centre, the order is E — L — Q — C. The line is written in the opposite direction, **C–Q–L**, from the corner towards the centre. This is how Lisovskaya reads it: the theme begins at the outer point and moves inwards along the spoke, towards money.

head: Position on the spoke
Letter
Label on our diagram
Example: 12.08.1992
rows: Centre of the chart · comfort zone

paragraphs: Our diagram uses numbers, letters and labels, with no icons. In the full reading, the line has its own ‘Material karma’ section, directly before ‘Money’. Its points are labelled Material task, Attitude to the material and Entry of the money line.
The money line runs from L: L → R2 → R. L therefore belongs to both lines, ending material karma and beginning the money line.

Other calculators often leave out the middle point, showing only C and L on the spoke. You can then calculate Q with a single addition. Some sites call the birth-year number alone material karma. Others use the term for the lower corners of the ancestral square, or for the karmic tail ‘read in terms of money’. The line described here is easy to identify: three numbers on the right-hand spoke, with **the middle number always equal to the reduced sum of the two outer numbers.** If that does not hold, you are looking at a different line or a different calculation method.

article_sections.h2: How to calculate material karma from your date of birth
paragraphs: The same rule applies to all three sums: **if a number is greater than 22, add its digits.** 31 → 3 + 1 = 4; 46 → 4 + 6 = 10. Keep 22 as it is: The Fool, the twenty-second arcanum. Let’s work through 12 August 1992.
**Step 1. The three numbers in the date.**

ul: **A — day:** 12. If the day is greater than 22, add its digits: 25 → 7, 31 → 4.
**B — month:** 8.
**C — year:** 1 + 9 + 9 + 2 = 21. This is the Material task. If the sum exceeds 22, add its digits again: 1987 → 25 → 7. The digits of 1984 add up to exactly 22, which stays 22.

paragraphs: **Step 2. The bottom corner and the centre.**

ul: **E = A + B + C + D** = 12 + 8 + 21 + 5 = 46 → 10. This is the centre of the chart.

paragraphs: **Step 3. Entry of the money line.** L = C + E = 21 + 10 = 31 → 4.
**Step 4. Attitude to the material.** Q = C + L = 21 + 4 = 25 → 7.
Material karma for 12.08.1992 is **21-7-4**: The World, The Chariot, The Emperor.

The main trap is the order. You calculate L first and Q second, but write the result C–Q–L. Writing the numbers in calculation order gives 21-4-7, which cannot be the material karma of any birth date: the middle number, 4, is not the reduced sum of the outer numbers.

paragraphs.h3: A quick check: add the two outer numbers

paragraphs: Calculated it by hand? Add the outer numbers and reduce the sum. You should get the middle number: 21 + 4 = 25 → 7. If you do not, check the centre and your digit sums. D is a common source of mistakes: an incorrect bottom point changes the centre, then L and Q.
Here are four dates to check your calculations against:

The second row needs no reduction at all. In the third, 22 remains The Fool; a calculator that subtracts 22 instead of adding digits would give 4 at the entry point instead of 8. In the fourth, the same number plays two different roles.

There are also quick ways to spot a mismatch. **Neither 1 nor 2 can appear at the middle or entry point, and 1 cannot appear at C.** Values of C from 2 to 4 occur only for people born from 2000 onwards; values from 13 to 22 occur only for people born before 2000. If your triple falls outside these limits, the calculator used different rules.

article_sections.h2: How material karma differs from the money channel, tail and family lines
paragraphs: Searches for ‘karma’ bring together several different ideas. The destiny matrix separates them into four lines:

head: Material karma
Money line
Karmic tail
Material family lines
rows: right-hand spoke, from the birth-year corner towards the centre
from entry point L to the crossing with the relationship line
lower spoke, from the centre towards the bottom corner
lower corners of the ancestral square
your attitude to material life: habitual ways of handling possessions, earnings and energy
non-material tasks: character, family and relationships with others
material themes in the male and female branches of the family

paragraphs: **One point shared with the money line.** The money line starts where material karma ends, and L is the same point on both lines for every birth date. Lisovskaya sees money as an extension of your attitude to material life: while you keep following the old material karma pattern, she says, the money line works in fits and starts. This is why ‘Material karma’ comes before ‘Money’ in the reading. The sections answer different questions, though: material karma concerns your habits around material things; money concerns the route through which you earn. On other diagrams, ‘under the dollar sign’ means R2, the middle of the money line. It does not refer to material karma.

**No points shared with the karmic tail.** Lisovskaya distinguishes material, spiritual and ancestral karmic tasks. She reads material tasks through material karma and spiritual tasks through the tail, and recommends looking at these two lines together. Their points are separate, however, even when the numbers match. Fifteen triples can occur as both a karmic tail and material karma. For example, 18-9-9 is one of the best-known tails, and 360 dates have the same material karma triple. The lines are written in opposite directions: the tail from the centre outwards, material karma from the outside in. The outer corner of the 18-9-9 tail holds 9; the outer corner of material karma 18-9-9 holds 18.

**No points shared with the family lines either.** ‘Ancestral material karma’ is a separate question, addressed by the lower corners of the ancestral square: Material male family line H and Material female family line I. The personal triple C–Q–L does not answer it. One more source of confusion: the compatibility chart has a point also labelled ‘Attitude to the material’. That point belongs to a chart for two people and is separate from your personal Q.

The neighbouring lines have their own guides: [Money in the destiny matrix](/encyclopedia/position/money), the [karmic tail](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail) and the material family lines — [Material male family line H](/encyclopedia/position/descendants) and [Material female family line I](/encyclopedia/position/inheritance).

article_sections.h2: The three roles: task, attitude and entry point
paragraphs: For Lisovskaya, ‘material’ extends beyond money. It includes earnings and work, property and possessions, housing, technology, transport, inheritance, physical activity and the bodily side of life — everything you can, as she puts it, ‘see, feel and touch’. She describes the line as expressing its negative side from birth. This is neither a curse nor a judgement: it means a pattern you follow until you recognise it. The task is to notice how the line’s energies show up in your life and find their strengths.

This is the main point on the line and the arcanum of your birth year. Lisovskaya writes that it sets the direction of the material theme: where and how your usual approach to material things lets you down. The other two points develop it.

C has a rarely mentioned feature: **it is the same for everyone born in the same year.** Everyone born in 1992 has The World here; everyone born in 1988 has Justice. C alone therefore tells you little about yourself as an individual. The personal detail begins with L: the entry point depends on the centre, and the centre depends on the whole date.

paragraphs.h3: Q — Attitude to the material: the mood

paragraphs: Lisovskaya calls this middle point the main point’s ‘helper’. It describes your mood around material things: how you relate to them, what you think and how you try to shape that part of your life. It is the inner voice you hear when you look at a price tag, a bank statement or someone else’s new car.

Two triples with the same C make the distinction clear. Both 21-7-4 and 21-6-3 have The World as their main point, with scale as the theme. With The Chariot at Q, however, prosperity is measured by progress: standing still means falling behind. With The Lovers, it is measured by choice and approval: both you and the people around you need to like what you have.

paragraphs.h3: L — Entry of the money line: an opening and a block

paragraphs: This is the last point, nearest the centre. Lisovskaya says its energy begins on its negative side but also opens the flow of money, so a person’s finances can lurch up and down. At L, the theme of C becomes a concrete action: taking on work, naming a price or deciding what to spend on. This is also where money gets stuck. The same point can open the way or block it, depending on how you express its energy.
Take The Chariot, number 7, and place it at each point in turn.

ul: **At C**, The Chariot makes movement the task. Your material affairs stay on track while you are moving towards a goal. Lisovskaya names the habitual negative expression plainly: erasing your personality, interests and desires for material gain. Everyone born in 1969, 1978, 1987, 1996, 2005, 2014 and 2023 has this C.
**At Q**, it is a mood. Prosperity is measured by progress: stopping feels like defeat, and a holiday feels like wasted time.
**At L**, it is the entry point. Money comes through projects, travel or a business of your own. It gets stuck when you have so much on the go that nothing reaches the finish line.

paragraphs: One card can describe three different people: someone who lives for the next result; someone who worries if a month passes without growth; someone who earns through movement but loses money in unfinished work. An arcanum’s meaning in material karma therefore always depends on its point.

paragraphs: A few points to bear in mind:

ul: **The Magician cannot occur at any point. The High Priestess occurs only at C, and only for people born in 2000.** A value of 1 at C would require a year whose digits add up to 1; there have been no such years since 1900. Q and L are sums of two numbers, one at least 2 and the other at least 3. Sums from 5 to 22 stay as they are; sums from 23 to 44 reduce to no less than 3 (30 → 3).

**The number at C reflects a birth year, rather than a rare gift.** Higher-numbered arcana, from 13 to 22, appear at C only for people born in the twentieth century. Lower numbers, from 2 to 4, occur only for those born from 2000 onwards.
**Numbers from 5 to 11 are the most common at Q and L**, each occurring for 7–10% of dates. Numbers from 12 to 20 appear at the middle point for 1–4% of dates: large sums reduce to small numbers.

**The number is not a score.** 22 is no ‘stronger’ than 3, and The Tower at the entry point is no ‘worse’ than The Empress. Every card at every point has both a strength and a habitual negative expression.

paragraphs: The roles of the points come from Lisovskaya. The key themes are our adaptation of her descriptions of the twenty-two energies to these three roles. Her book describes the energies in general, without separate meanings for each point on this line.

article_sections.h2: Material karma 9, 11 and other numbers: find the point first
paragraphs: The most common searches use a single number: ‘material karma 9’, ‘material karma 11’. A number alone, however, does not tell you where it sits. A 9 can be the main theme, the mood or the entry point, giving you three different answers.

These percentages cover all dates from 1900 onwards. The key point is clear: **9 and 11 appear at the middle and entry points twice as often as at the main point.** So the first response to ‘what does material karma 9 mean?’ is another question: at which point?

ul: **At C** — for people born in 1989, 1998, 2007, 2016 and 2025. The theme is independence and depth in material life: your own work, your own expertise, your own pace. The habitual negative expression is to withdraw, trust no one and carry everything alone.
**At Q** — a mood of caution. Money is kept quiet and put aside ‘just in case’; other people’s offers are met with suspicion.
**At L** — an entry through specialist knowledge and work you do yourself. The block: your knowledge stays hidden, you never name a price and you never take your offer to anyone.

**At C** — for people born in 1901, 1910, 2009 and 2018. The theme is strength and stamina: the capacity to carry a load others could not manage. The habitual negative expression is to work yourself into the ground and force matters that could be settled by agreement.
**At Q** — an ‘I’ll manage on my own’ mood. When your energy runs out, your view of money becomes narrower and bleaker.

**At L** — an entry through work, endurance and leadership. The block is relentless pressure: taking on more and more, unable to stop and rest. In her 8-19-11 example, Lisovskaya describes Strength at the entry point in stark terms: thinking is ‘negative, limited and narrow’, with insufficient self-control.

paragraphs: For the other numbers — 21, 8, 6, 10, 7 and 4 — use the relevant row in the table above, reading each cell in its own column. 21 appears most often at C: The World is the Material task for everyone born in 1929, 1938, 1947, 1956, 1965, 1974, 1983 and 1992.

article_sections.h2: How to read the three numbers together
paragraphs: Three themes in a row are still short of a reading. ‘The World: scale. The Chariot: prosperity as progress. The Emperor: responsibility.’ That is a glossary, leaving the reader to supply the connections. A reading begins when the three cards form a single idea.

ol: **Start with C.** It sets the theme: what your material life is about. Read the other points as answers to the question it raises.
**Look at how Q colours the theme.** This is the mood you bring to C: anxiety, excitement, shame or calm.
**Find how L turns the theme into money.** How money comes in, and where the very same trait stops it.

**Work out how the cards relate to one another.** They may support each other: The Emperor at C and Justice at the entry point mean order supported by clear agreements. They may clash: The Fool at C and The Emperor at L mean freedom that must take a structured form before money comes in. They may unfold in sequence: The Hanged Man followed by The Chariot means a long wait followed by a burst of action.
**Write one sentence about yourself.** Begin with ‘I’, rather than ‘these cards mean’: ‘I take on big projects, but I want to handle every detail myself.’
**Find where the same logic gets in your way.** The line’s difficulty grows out of its strength. Someone who knows how to endure can easily start enduring a lack of money.

**Check it against a real situation.** Your last major purchase; your last conversation about a price. If nothing feels familiar, do not force a fit: this may be a less prominent part of your life at present.

paragraphs: Order matters. 21-6-3 and 3-6-21 contain the same numbers but describe different lines. In the first, The World is the theme and The Empress the entry point: a large-scale task that turns into money through care and things that grow. In the second, the roles are reversed: the theme is nurturing and protecting what is yours, and the entry point is a wider reach you feel afraid to pursue. The first triple occurs for 320 dates; the second for just 14, all in 2001 and 2010.

The texts in the full reading follow this approach. Each of the 246 triples has its own title, captions for the three cards and three paragraphs: the theme, how it looks in life, and the difficulty, with a question to ask yourself and one manageable step. Two of these texts appear in full below.

article_sections.h2: Lisovskaya’s worked example: Justice, The Sun and Strength
paragraphs: Lisovskaya uses this triple in Matritsa Sudby dlya nachinayushchikh (The Destiny Matrix for Beginners) to demonstrate how to read the line. The book gives no birth date, but you can check the calculation with 06.01.1988: C = 8, centre = 3, L = 8 + 3 = 11, Q = 8 + 11 = 19. This material karma occurs for 0.39% of dates, roughly 1 in 257. It appears among people born in 1979, 1988, 1997, 2006, 2015 and 2024.

**Where the idea comes from.** Lisovskaya takes a stricter view of 8-19-11. For her, 8 at the main point concerns law and honesty in money matters. The neighbouring 19 means that a person **‘scatters their potential excessively, taking on everything at once’**; together with 8, it puts them **‘in pursuit of a beautiful and wealthy life’**. Strength at the entry point is **‘an opening and a block at the same time’**: in her account, their thinking lacks self-control. She sees a way forward in planning expenses, self-discipline and an honest path. Her list of negative expressions of 8 includes extreme possibilities, extending to illegal earnings. These are possible expressions of an energy, rather than conclusions about a person, so they have been left out of the reading. What remains is the mechanism: wanting a dazzling life demands more and more of your energy, and you can test that idea against a celebration of your own.

article_sections.h2: Our worked example: The World, The Chariot and The Emperor
paragraphs: We calculated this triple above using 12.08.1992. It also occurs for 01.01.1992 and another 39 dates that year. Across the full date range it occurs for 328 dates, or 0.71%, roughly 1 in 141, among people born in 1929, 1938, 1947, 1956, 1965, 1974, 1983 and 1992. There is another detail: all these dates have the same karmic tail, 15-20-5. Lisovskaya discusses it in the same book as a ‘common’ tail, writing it in reverse as 5-20-15. She recommends reading material karma alongside the tail, and here the pairing stays the same.

**Where the idea comes from.** The World, in Lisovskaya’s book, stands for ‘citizens of the world’ and working on a global scale; its negative side is withdrawal, rigid views and an inability to accept other people. Her advice for this energy is to **‘overcome your fear of expansion and global projects’**. For The Chariot, she names a common negative expression as **‘erasing your personality, interests or desires for material gain’** — hence prosperity measured only by progress. She advises The Emperor to **‘understand that you cannot be responsible for everything’**. In this triple, the three ideas converge: a big undertaking needs other people, while the entry point tests whether you are willing to trust them with anything at all.

Four triples appear most often alongside ‘material karma’ in the search data: 12-19-7 — 18 searches a month; 4-17-13 — 13; 20-11-9 — 12; 5-15-10 — 11 (Wordstat, 08.09–07.10.2026). Two more contain a repeated number: 9-9-18 and 18-9-9. Below is the connecting idea for each triple, and the point where it starts to get in the way. The full texts, with captions for all three cards, are in the reading.

paragraphs.h3: 12-19-7 · The Hanged Man, The Sun, The Chariot

paragraphs: First, check the line. This is the most searched-for triple, yet one of the rarest as material karma: just 36 dates, nine each in 1902, 1911, 1920 and 2019 (22.04.2019, 21.05.2019, 20.06.2019 and so on each month). By contrast, 12-19-7 is one of the most common karmic tails, occurring for 9% of dates. Reversed, 7-19-12 is a material karma triple found among people born in 1969, 1978, 1987 and subsequent years at nine-year intervals. Make sure you know which line you have and which way it is written. If it really is C–Q–L, The Hanged Man as the theme concerns learning to charge for your work; the old habit is to work for a thank-you and leave your own reward for later. The Sun as the mood expects a dazzling life of plenty, all at once. The Chariot at the entry point brings money through movement and projects. **A long stretch of putting up with things gives way to a rush for everything at once.** The vulnerable point is compensation: after working unpaid for so long, you want to grab the first quick project, and once again rush into it on someone else’s terms.

The Emperor as the theme: material life rests on order and responsibility for what is yours; the old habit is control and wanting to take more than you give. The Star as the mood: dreaming of your own venture and recognition, trusting that your talent will be valued. Death at the entry point: money comes through change — a new job, clearing out the old, a different way of working. **Order should serve the dream, rather than take its place.** The Emperor builds a system, The Star wants to shine within it, and the entry point tests whether you can close things down when they have run their course. The vulnerable point is holding on to something secure that stopped bringing you joy long ago: the dream waits ‘until things are stable’, but stability never arrives, even though change is precisely what opens the way to money for this triple. It occurs for 0.24% of dates, only among people born in 2002, 2011 and 2020, for example 13.01.2002.

Judgement as the theme: material life is tied to family, legacy and what was said about money at home; the old habit is inherited beliefs and judging other people’s money. Strength as the mood: ‘I’ll manage on my own.’ The Hermit at the entry point: money comes through deep expertise and solitary work. **You handle money and practical matters alone, as though someone is judging how well you cope.** At its best, this combination gives you stamina and knowledge to rely on. Its vulnerable point is silence: asking for help or a pay rise feels like defeat, the price goes unspoken, and exhaustion builds until Strength has no strength left. Around 0.8% of dates, among people born in 1919, 1928 and every nine years thereafter up to 1991, for example 05.01.1982.

paragraphs.h3: 5-15-10 · The Hierophant, The Devil, The Wheel of Fortune

paragraphs: The Hierophant as the theme: material life rests on rules, knowledge and ‘the right way’. The Devil as the mood: strong desire, a passion for quality and luxury, temptation. The Wheel of Fortune at the entry point: money comes through a chance seized in time, then goes straight back into a repeating cycle. **The rules say ‘you mustn’t’, desire says ‘I want to’, and chance decides.** The vulnerable point is the cycle: strict rules, giving in to temptation, guilt, even stricter rules — and The Wheel of Fortune turns again. The strength of this triple lies in looking honestly at your own desire: a rule that takes account of what you want is easier to keep than an outright ban. Around 0.8% of dates, among people born in 1949, 1958, 1967, 1976, 1985, 1994, 2003, 2012 and 2021, for example 10.01.1976.

paragraphs.h3: 9-9-18 · The Hermit, The Hermit, The Moon

paragraphs: Two 9s play two different roles; they do not simply mean ‘twice as withdrawn’. The Hermit as the theme is independence: your own work, your own pace, reliance on yourself. The Hermit as the mood is caution: keeping money quiet, saving just in case, distrusting other people’s offers. The Moon at the entry point brings money through imagination and understanding people, while fear blocks it. **You prepare alone for so long that fear has time to invent the rejection.** The vulnerable point is work nobody sees: you keep it to yourself, imagining how it will be rejected, and the prospect of earning stays hazy. Around 0.4% of dates, among people born in 1989, 1998, 2007, 2016 and 2025. For 09.09.1989, this triple also repeats the talent line — more on that below.

paragraphs.h3: 18-9-9 · The Moon, The Hermit, The Hermit

paragraphs: These are the same numbers as the best-known karmic tail, but here they form material karma, read in a different order. The Moon is the theme rather than the entry point: material life is wrapped in anxiety and imagined scenarios, with fear of loss and uncertainty about the figures as the old habit. The Hermit as the mood is caution; The Hermit at the entry point brings money through expertise and independent work. **Fear paints a picture worse than reality, and you go to check it alone.** In 9-9-18, fear sits at the point where money comes in; in 18-9-9, it colours the whole theme from the start. The vulnerable point is never reaching out: you check your bill, your price and your project only against your own anxiety. Around 0.8% of dates, among people born in 1908, 1917 and every nine years thereafter up to 1980, for example 08.01.1980.

article_sections.h2: How many material karma triples are there, and how common is yours?
paragraphs: We checked all 46,333 dates from 1 January 1900 to 8 November 2026 and found **246 distinct material karma triples**. Half occur for more than 192 dates, and half for fewer. Forty-six triples occur for fewer than 50 dates; eleven for fewer than ten.

paragraphs: The Sun at C takes the top eight places, for a reason. It appears at C for people born in ten different years — 1909, 1918 and so on up to 1990 — more years than any other arcanum. **How common a material karma triple is depends above all on the birth year.** Within a single year there are only 9 to 15 triples, and the most common belongs to roughly 1 in 8 dates that year. Two dates from the same year produce the same material karma roughly 1 time in 10. Two random dates from all 127 years match in 6 cases out of 1,000.
The calculation also revealed the following:

ul: **The rarest triple is 4-21-17**, The Emperor, The World, The Star. It appeared only three times: 22.12.2002, 22.12.2011 and 22.12.2020. The triple 9-13-4 occurs only on 1 January, in 1989, 1998, 2007, 2016 and 2025.

**Two adjacent numbers can match only beside The Moon.** C and Q match only when 18 is at the entry point: 5-5-18, 6-6-18 and so on up to 11-11-18. Q and L match only when 18 is at C: from 18-5-5 to 18-11-11. The outer numbers match in just three triples: 5-10-5, 6-12-6 and 7-14-7. Three identical numbers never occur.

**Reversing the order creates a different triple.** In 71 pairs, both orders are possible: C–Q–L and the same set with the outer numbers swapped. Each member of these pairs has its own reading, because the main theme and entry point exchange roles.

article_sections.h2: The same material karma, different people
paragraphs: Only two things determine the triple: your birth year and the centre of the chart. These match for 12.08.1992 and 01.01.1992, so both dates have material karma 21-7-4. Even the tail matches. The rest of the chart differs, though: the talent line is 8-8-18 for the first date and 1-12-11 for the second, with different days, months and everything calculated from them. Two people with the same triple therefore receive the same automated reading, while its relationship to the other lines becomes clear only in the context of the whole chart.
Lisovskaya recommends checking whether material karma ‘mirrors’ another line. The calculation shows when this happens:

ul: **With the talent line** B–P–K, material karma matches exactly when the birth-year arcanum equals the month number. For example, 1988 gives C = 8, so everyone born in August 1988 has identical material karma and talent lines. This occurs for 3.6% of dates. Lisovskaya believes that in such cases talents cannot develop fully until the tasks of the material line have been addressed. That is her experience in practice, rather than a rule the calculation can verify.
**With the karmic tail**, a match occurs when C equals the bottom corner D. Material karma then repeats the tail read from the corner towards the centre. This occurs for 2.6% of dates.

paragraphs: The clearest example is 09.09.1989. Material karma is 9-9-18, the talent line is 9-9-18 and the tail is 18-9-9: three lines built from the same numbers, with a different role for each number on each line.

article_sections.h2: What material karma cannot tell you
paragraphs: ‘Karma’ can sound like a verdict, and ‘material’ like an income forecast. This line gives you neither.

ul: **How much you will earn.** The triple describes habits around material life, rather than a bank balance. People with very different levels of wealth can have the same material karma.

**Debts, dishonesty or ‘bad karma’.** Lisovskaya’s lists of negative expressions include some serious possibilities. These are potential expressions of an energy, rather than conclusions about a particular person.
**Past lives.** The connection with past incarnations is the author’s belief. A birth date proves nothing about how someone lived before.
**How you feel physically.** Physical activity belongs to the material theme, but these numbers cannot support conclusions about your body or wellbeing.
**Your ancestry.** The paternal and maternal lines play no part in calculating C–Q–L. Material themes in the family belong to points H and I.
**A verdict of ‘negative from birth’.** This describes a starting point, rather than a judgement. Each point’s strength grows from the same energy as its habitual negative expression.

**Changes over time.** The numbers stay the same because the birth date stays the same. What changes is how you express your triple. Lisovskaya writes that the line’s tasks return throughout life and become easier each time you handle them successfully. The calculation contains no ritual for ‘clearing’ material karma.

article_sections.h2: Try it for yourself: a week of money decisions
paragraphs: Material karma shows up in small things: a purchase, a conversation about a price, the way you use your possessions and energy. An ordinary week gives you a chance to notice it.

ol: **Write down the three key themes** for your triple from the table above, each in its own column.

**For seven evenings, write three lines.** What repeated itself today in how I handled money, possessions or energy? What was I thinking and feeling at the time? What happened when I needed to name a price, accept money or spend it?
**After a week, compare your notes with the themes.** The first line relates to C, the second to Q and the third to L.
**Find one situation where the habit helped and one where it got in the way.** Usually, it is the same trait in two different settings.
**Ask someone close to you:** ‘How do I behave when I have money to spare? What about when I need to ask for payment?’ An outside view can sometimes be more accurate than your own.

paragraphs: If the week bears no resemblance to the themes, do not force it to fit. Another line may be more prominent at present, such as the money line or the tail.

The free calculation shows your diagram with Q between C and L, along with your triple and the role of each point. This article explains what each arcanum means in each role; explanations of the points in your own triple become available when you unlock the section.
The full reading adds a ‘Material karma’ section before ‘Money’. It reads your triple as a whole:

ul: a title that captures the combination’s central idea;
a caption for each of the three cards, explaining its role at that point;
three paragraphs: the line’s theme and each card’s contribution, how it looks in life, and the difficulty, with a question to ask yourself and one step to test it.

paragraphs: Each of the 246 triples has its own text, like the examples for 8-19-11 and 21-7-4 above. The ‘Money’ section follows, continuing from the same point L. If you want to connect material karma to your whole chart and explore a specific question, that is the work of an individual reading.

ul: **Formulas** — the classic destiny matrix: C is the reduced sum of the digits of the birth year; D = A + B + C; centre E = A + B + C + D; L = C + E; Q = C + L. Sums above 22 are reduced by adding digits; 22 is kept. All figures in this article come from running the calculator engine across 46,333 dates, from 1 January 1900 to 8 November 2026: 246 triples, their frequencies, impossible numbers, repetitions and matches with the tail and talent lines.

**Point roles and how to read the line** — Yuliana Lisovskaya, Matritsa Sudby dlya nachinayushchikh (The Destiny Matrix for Beginners): the meanings of points and lines, in the chapters ‘What Material Karma Is and How Points Are Integrated’, ‘The Influence of Material Karma’ and ‘Integrating Lines and Points’. The 8-19-11 example comes from the same book. The author uses her own point numbers and letters: our C is her point 6, Q is 14 and L is 15; the birth year is labelled with the Cyrillic letter Ve. The correspondence was established from the points’ positions on the diagram and the label ‘entry to the finance line’.

**Arcanum meanings** — Lisovskaya’s descriptions of the twenty-two energies. The key themes for the three roles and the combination readings are our own adaptation. Past incarnations and lists of negative expressions reflect the author’s beliefs and practice; they have been left out of the readings.

**The name ‘material karma’** refers to C–Q–L in Lisovskaya’s work. Other schools and calculators apply it to other points too, so compare numbers on other sites by their positions on the diagram, rather than by the name alone.
The destiny matrix is an esoteric framework for self-observation with no scientific evidence base. It provides neither financial advice nor an income forecast.

paragraphs: **Look at the right-hand spoke of your chart.** Enter your date of birth to see your three numbers between the birth-year corner and the centre: theme, mood and entry point. The full reading brings them together, then the next section follows the same point L into money.

faq.q: Where on the diagram do I find material karma?
faq.a: On the right-hand spoke, from the birth-year corner C towards the centre. It has three points: C at the outside, Q in the middle and L nearest the centre. Our diagram labels them ‘Material task’, ‘Attitude to the material’ and ‘Entry of the money line’. In the reading, the line has its own section before ‘Money’. Other calculators often leave out the middle point; you can calculate it by adding the two outer numbers.

faq.q: Can I work out material karma by hand, without a calculator?
faq.a: Add the digits of your birth year to get C. Work out the centre: D = day + month + C, E = day + month + C + D. Then L = C + E and Q = C + L. Reduce every sum above 22 by adding its digits. For example, 12.08.1992 gives C = 21, E = 10, L = 31 → 4, Q = 25 → 7: material karma 21-7-4.

faq.q: Is material karma the arcanum of my birth year?
faq.a: The birth-year arcanum is only the first point, C. It is the same for everyone born that year, so C alone cannot describe you as an individual. Lisovskaya reads material karma through three points: C sets the theme, Q and L develop it, and L also opens the money line.

First, find which point holds the 9. At C, it is a theme of independence and depth, with a habit of withdrawing. At Q, it is caution and silence about money. At L, it is an entry through specialist knowledge, blocked by an unspoken price. A 9 occurs at the middle and entry points twice as often as at C.

faq.q: Is material karma 11 good or bad?
faq.a: The meaning depends on the point; the numbers themselves are neither good nor bad. At C, it is strength and stamina, with a habit of working yourself into the ground. At Q, it is an ‘I’ll manage on my own’ mood that narrows your view of money when you are tired. At L, money comes through work and endurance, while relentless pressure without rest blocks it. Like 9, 11 occurs more often at Q and L than at C.

faq.q: Why does another calculator give me different material karma?
faq.a: Usually for one of four reasons. It calls the birth-year number alone material karma. It leaves out the middle point, showing only C and L. It writes the line from the centre outwards, L–Q–C: the same numbers in reverse. Or it reduces sums above 22 by subtracting 22 instead of adding digits, turning 26 into 4 rather than 8. Some schools also use ‘material karma’ for the lower corners of the ancestral square or for the tail. Compare the rules and the points’ positions before comparing interpretations.

faq.q: I was given ‘material karma 12 19 7’. Why are your numbers different?
faq.a: 12-19-7 is the most common triple in the search data, but as C–Q–L it occurs for only 36 dates, in 1902, 1911, 1920 and 2019. It is, however, one of the most common karmic tails. Reversed, 7-19-12 is a material karma triple found among people born in 1969, 1978, 1987 and every nine years thereafter. Check which line you have and which direction it is written in.

faq.q: How does material karma differ from the money channel?
faq.a: They are two lines with one shared point. Material karma C–Q–L describes habits around material life: possessions, earnings and energy. The money line L–R2–R describes how income comes to you. L ends the first and begins the second, so Lisovskaya reads them as a continuation of each other. On other diagrams, ‘under the dollar sign’ refers to R2, the middle of the money line, rather than any material karma point.

faq.q: Are material karma and the karmic tail the same thing?
faq.a: No. The tail is the lower spoke, M–N–D, sharing no points with the right-hand spoke. Lisovskaya recommends reading both lines together: the tail concerns non-material tasks, material karma concerns material ones. Fifteen triples can occur as both, such as 18-9-9, but the tail is written from the centre outwards and material karma from the corner inwards.

That is a separate question. Material themes in the male and female branches of the family belong to the lower corners of the ancestral square, points H and I. Personal material karma C–Q–L is calculated without the family points and does not answer questions about ancestry.

faq.q: Can I work through or clear my material karma?
faq.a: The numbers stay the same because they are calculated from your birth date. Lisovskaya writes that this line’s tasks return throughout life, becoming easier each time if you handle them and learn to act from the strengths of your energies. The calculation offers no ritual that will ‘clear’ the triple and bring money.

faq.q: Can material karma be good or bad?
faq.a: No. The numbers identify cards; they are not scores. ‘Negative from birth’ means starting with a habitual pattern, rather than being given a bad triple. Each combination has its own strength and difficulty, both growing from the same energies.

faq.q: Is material karma different for men and women?
faq.a: No. Sex plays no part in the calculation: a man and a woman born on the same day have the same triple.

faq.q: Why can 1 and 2 never appear at the middle or entry point?
faq.a: It comes down to arithmetic. L is the sum of C and the centre, which are at least 2 and 3 respectively. Q is the sum of C and L. Sums up to 22 stay as they are and cannot be below 5; sums from 23 to 44 reduce to no less than 3. Nor can 1 occur at C: no year from 1900 to 2026 has digits that add up to 1.

The destiny matrix uses Marseille numbering: 8 is Justice, 11 is Strength and 22 is The Fool. Waite and many Tarot books swap 8 and 11. The meaning belongs to the card’s name, so when using another reference, match interpretations by name rather than number.
